goal.en: Plays Melodie, Op. 68 No. 1, by Robert Schumann with a singing melody over a quiet accompaniment.
goal.tr: Robert Schumann'ın Melodie'sini (Op. 68 No. 1) sessiz bir eşlik üstünde şarkı söyler gibi bir ezgiyle çalar.

explanation.en: Robert Schumann (1810–1856) wrote Album for the Young, Op. 68, in 1848 for his daughters. Melodie is the first piece.
explanation.tr: Robert Schumann (1810–1856) Gençlik Albümü'nü (Op. 68) 1848'de kızları için yazdı. Melodie ilk parçadır.

explanation.en: The right hand sings the melody. The left hand plays a calm line below it, and the hands often start notes together.
explanation.tr: Sağ el ezgiyi söyler. Sol el altında sakin bir çizgi çalar; eller sık sık birlikte nota başlatır.

explanation.en: It is in C major and 4/4, 20 bars long. The left hand plays eighth notes almost all the way; the right hand mostly plays quarter notes, with a few two-note chords.
explanation.tr: Do majör ve 4/4'lüktür, 20 ölçü sürer. Sol el neredeyse baştan sona sekizlik çalar; sağ el çoğunlukla dörtlük çalar, birkaç yerde iki notalı akor vardır.

explanation.en: Play legato and let the melody sound above the left hand.
explanation.tr: Legato çal ve ezginin sol elin üstünde duyulmasını sağla.

explanation.en: There is no target tempo. Choose a calm tempo at which every note is clear.
explanation.tr: Hedef tempo yok. Her notanın net olduğu sakin bir tempo seç.

explanation.en: The microphone result here is experimental: it does not lock your progress. With a MIDI keyboard the result is exact.
explanation.tr: Buradaki mikrofon sonucu deneyseldir: ilerlemeni kilitlemez. MIDI klavyeyle sonuç kesindir.

brief.en: Melodie, Op. 68 No. 1, from the Ostinato edition: melody alone, then both hands, calm and legato, piano synthesis.
brief.tr: Ostinato düzenlemesinden Melodie, Op. 68 No. 1: önce yalnız ezgi, sonra iki el, sakin ve legato, piyano sentezi.

task.en: Play the right hand alone once, then the left hand. Then play the piece with both hands at a calm, steady tempo, without the repeat of bars 1–4.
task.tr: Sağ eli bir kez tek başına, sonra sol eli çal. Sonra parçayı iki elle, 1–4. ölçülerin tekrarı olmadan, sakin ve düzenli bir tempoda çal.

selfCheck.en: The melody was louder than the accompaniment.
The notes were connected, with no gaps.
Notes meant to start together started together.
selfCheck.tr: Birlikte başlaması gereken notalar birlikte başladı.

selfCheck.en: My shoulders and wrists stayed loose.

fix.en: The hands drift apart. Play the two bars around the slip slowly and press both keys at the same moment.
fix.tr: Eller birbirinden kayıyor. Kaçışın çevresindeki iki ölçüyü yavaş çal ve iki tuşa aynı anda bas.

fix.en: Find a quieter spot and keep the phone about an arm's length away.
fix.tr: Daha sessiz bir yer bul ve telefonu yaklaşık bir kol boyu uzakta tut.

adaptation.en: Play the melody with only the first left-hand note of each bar.
adaptation.tr: Ezgiyi, her ölçüde sol elin yalnız ilk notasıyla çal.

repertoire: Robert Schumann (1810–1856), Album für die Jugend, Op. 68 No. 1, "Melodie" (composed 1848; C major, 4/4, 20 bars). Source edition: Erstes Album für die Jugend, Op. 68, new teaching edition arranged progressively with fingering by Karl Klauser, Leipzig: J. Schuberth & Co., [1867], plate 4359, p. 3; scan: Gaylord Music Library, Washington University in St. Louis, https://archive.org/details/b26976821 (Public Domain Mark 1.0). Klauser's fingering is not used. Not yet compared with the 1848 Schuberth first edition. Both hands, without the repeat of bars 1–4; the sequence lists every note start, notes starting together joined with '/' (right-hand chords in bars 4, 9, 11, 17 and 19; in bars 8 and 16 the upper F5 is held while the lower voice moves). Every bar was checked twice against the scan (pitches and rhythm). Public domain: composer died 1856; edition published 1867; Klauser died 1905. Legal review pending. Notation, fingering and tempo by Ostinato.
